stories.head: Madras High Court bars Blinkit from using a CSK superfan's look in ads; the fan wants ₹1.1 crore in damages
stories.dek: Chennai fan Saravanan Hari says a Blinkit newspaper cartoon copied his famous yellow match-day look and made people think he was promoting the app.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Madras High Court has stopped Blink Commerce, which runs Blinkit, from using the likeness of Chennai Super Kings superfan Saravanan Hari without his written consent. Justice P B Balaji said the cartoon and the fan looked alike at first glance.

The fight is over a full-page Blinkit ad in a Chennai newspaper in March 2025, with the line 'The men in yellow always deliver'. In one corner was a cartoon fan with yellow body paint, curly hair, a thick moustache, 'THALA 7' on his chest and a double thumbs-up.

sections.title: The fan's side
paras: Saravanan says he has used this exact look since around 2013, and it is well known from TV, newspapers, brand deals, a nod from MS Dhoni and a cameo in the Tamil film GOAT. He says friends and fans asked him if he had signed up with Blinkit.
He wants ₹1.1 crore in damages and a ruling that his look is his own property.

sections.title: Blinkit's side and what's next
paras: In reply to his legal notice, Blinkit said the cartoon was fictional and had nothing to do with him, but said it would stop using the character as a goodwill gesture.

The court also told Blinkit and the newspaper's publisher to keep all the ad's design files and emails. The next hearing is on 14 December. It is a reminder to brands that 'inspired by' a famous fan can land in court, and it comes the same week Dhoni ended his IPL playing career.

facts: Ad ran in March 2025 with the line 'The men in yellow always deliver'
Fan is seeking ₹1.1 crore in damages

stories.head: Ranveer Singh and boAt's Aman Gupta launch H.I.M, a men's grooming brand with 8 products priced ₹299–₹899
stories.dek: H.I.M stands for 'Handsome Indian Man'. Ranveer is a co-founder, not just the face, and the brand says its range is made for Indian skin, weather and hard water.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Actor Ranveer Singh and boAt co-founder Aman Gupta launched H.I.M (Handsome Indian Man) on 17 November. It starts with eight products across face, body and hair: face wash, moisturiser, sunscreen, body wash, body lotion, a soap bar, a 2-in-1 shampoo and a scalp serum.
Prices run from ₹299 to ₹899. You can buy them on the brand's own website, Amazon and Blinkit.

sections.title: The pitch
paras: The founders say most grooming products sold to Indian men were made for other markets. H.I.M claims its formulas are built for heat, humidity, pollution and hard water, and every product uses an in-house ingredient it calls IN·XT, meant to help the skincare soak in better.

Ranveer said he worked with scientists from the first samples to the final products. Aman said Indian men now read labels and build routines, and pointed to an 850% jump in searches for men's skincare routines over five years.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Unlike most celebrity brands, Ranveer is a co-founder here, not a paid ambassador. The launch is part of Aman's venture studio OFF/BEAT, which raised ₹100 crore in April from Bessemer Venture Partners.

The market is growing fast: IMARC Group expects India's men's grooming market to grow from $2.62 billion in 2026 to $4.46 billion by 2034. H.I.M walks into a busy aisle that already has Beardo, The Man Company, Bombay Shaving Company and Tiger Shroff's Prowl.

facts: Sold on its website, Amazon and Blinkit
Men's grooming market: $2.62B (2026) to $4.46B (2034), per IMARC

stories.head: MS Dhoni retires from IPL cricket after 278 matches and 5,439 runs; he will be Chennai Super Kings' Team Mentor from IPL 2027
stories.dek: CSK announced the news on retention day, ending a 19-year playing career that brought Chennai five titles. There will be no farewell match at Chepauk.

sections.title: What happened
paras: On Tuesday, 17 November, the deadline for IPL teams to submit their retention lists, Chennai Super Kings said on X that MS Dhoni 'takes charge as the Team Mentor'. He has stepped away as a player and will guide the team from IPL 2027.

The decision came quietly, only hours before the deadline. Cricbuzz reported that even people inside CSK learned of it only on Tuesday. CSK said he 'will always be a part of our identity' and that Chennai 'will always be his home'.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Dhoni ends with 278 IPL matches, 5,439 runs and 24 fifties. As captain he led CSK to five titles: 2010, 2011, 2018, 2021 and 2023. His last IPL season was 2025, when CSK kept him as an 'uncapped' player for ₹4 crore. Harsha Bhogle called it 'the end of an era'.

sections.title: Other retention-day moves
paras: It was a busy day across the league. Mohammed Shami moved from Lucknow Super Giants to Rajasthan Royals for ₹8 crore. Arshdeep Singh went to Mumbai Indians for ₹18 crore. Liam Livingstone joined CSK for ₹6 crore. Kuldeep Yadav moved to Lucknow for ₹13.5 crore, and Kolkata now need a new captain after Ajinkya Rahane's exit.

sections.title: What's next
paras: The IPL 2027 mini-auction is in Goa on 16 December. As mentor, Dhoni is expected to have a big say in how CSK rebuild.

stories.head: Nvidia's sales double to $115.8 billion in its first results without Jensen Huang, but the board says he won't be coming back
stories.dek: The AI chip giant beat Wall Street's estimates and raised its outlook. Huang said he would be 'honored' to return, but Nvidia's board quickly shut the door.
stat: Nvidia revenue in one quarter, up 103%

sections.title: What happened
paras: Nvidia reported results for the July–October quarter on Tuesday, 17 November. Revenue came in at $115.8 billion, more than double the $57 billion it made a year earlier, and well above the roughly $109 billion analysts expected.
Its data-centre business, which sells the chips that power AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude, made $107.6 billion of that, up 110% from a year ago.

sections.title: The Huang question
paras: This was Nvidia's first results call since co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO last week. Hours earlier, Huang said in a post on X that he would be 'honored' to return if the board felt it was best for shareholders.

The board's answer came on the call itself. Chair Harvey Jones said the board accepted his resignation unanimously and 'does not intend to reinstate' him. It is now searching for a permanent CEO, while finance chief Colette Kress runs the company for now.

sections.title: What's next
paras: Nvidia expects $127.4–132.6 billion in revenue next quarter, again above forecasts, and announced a $150 billion share buyback. Kress called it 'business as usual' and said the company's cloud order backlog has grown to $2.5 trillion. Shares rose in after-hours trading.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Nvidia's numbers are a mood check for the whole AI boom. Strong results ease fears that AI spending is slowing, just a day before Anthropic is set to list on Nasdaq.

facts: Revenue: $115.8 billion, up 103% from a year ago

stories.head: Perplexity could file for a US IPO as early as early 2027, says Aravind Srinivas, as its yearly revenue run rate hits $1 billion
stories.dek: The Chennai-born CEO had earlier said Perplexity would not go public before 2028. Faster growth has changed the plan, with India its biggest market by users.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas told CNBC that the AI search company could file for a US stock market listing as soon as the first quarter of 2027. 'I wouldn't rule out filing something' in early 2027, he said, because the business is growing faster than expected.
That is a big change. Earlier, Srinivas had said Perplexity would not list before 2028.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: Perplexity's annual recurring revenue, the yearly value of its subscriptions, has reached $1 billion. The company had expected about $750 million by the time of an IPO.
The app has been downloaded more than 80 million times.
Srinivas co-founded Perplexity in 2022 with Denis Yarats, Johnny Ho and Andy Konwinski. In June 2026, Tech Mahindra rolled out Perplexity's enterprise product across its sales teams.

sections.title: The India angle
paras: India is Perplexity's largest market. A deal with Airtel gave its 360 million users a free year of Perplexity Pro, and downloads peaked at 22 million in October 2025. After the offer ended, downloads fell to about 14 million by July 2026.

Indians have not paid much yet: estimated monthly revenue from India rose from $34,000 in January 2025 to $156,000 in July 2026, according to TechCrunch figures quoted by Inc42. The IPO talk comes as AI companies line up to list, with Anthropic set to debut on Nasdaq this week.

facts: ARR $1 billion vs. $750 million expected before IPO
Airtel deal offered free Pro to 360 million users

stories.head: Urban Company's ₹2,500 crore share sale is oversubscribed about 6 times; SBI MF, ICICI Prudential, Goldman Sachs and Norges bid
stories.dek: Big investors rushed in on day one. Urban Company will use ₹600 crore of the money to fight Snabbit and Pronto in the 'maid in minutes' race.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Urban Company's ₹2,500 crore QIP, a share sale only for big institutions, drew bids worth about six times the amount on offer, Moneycontrol reported on 17 November. The floor price was ₹161.03 a share.

Bidders included SBI, ICICI Prudential, UTI, Aditya Birla Sun Life, Mirae and Invesco mutual funds, insurers HDFC Life and Bajaj Life, and long-term global funds like Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Norway's Norges and Amundi.

sections.title: Where the money goes
paras: About ₹600 crore, roughly a quarter, is set aside for InstaHelp, the app's quick home-help service for cleaning and dishwashing. Rivals Snabbit (backed by Lightspeed) and Pronto (backed by General Catalyst) are spending heavily on discounts too.

Urban Company has said it will put market share ahead of short-term profit in InstaHelp. Moneycontrol notes it has burned more cash in one quarter than Snabbit did in a full year. Snabbit lost ₹167.75 crore in FY26 on just ₹12.25 crore of revenue.

sections.title: The bigger trend
paras: Listed new-age companies keep coming back to big investors for money. Together they have raised or announced more than ₹25,200 crore through QIPs since 2021. Zomato raised ₹8,500 crore this way in 2024 and Swiggy ₹10,000 crore in 2025.

A QIP lets a listed company raise money quickly without a fresh public offer. For Urban Company, strong demand from big funds is a vote of confidence in its bet that Indians will book house help as easily as they order groceries.

facts: QIP size ₹2,500 crore at a floor price of ₹161.03
New-age firms have raised ₹25,200 crore+ via QIPs since 2021

stories.head: OpenAI launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol; Astra is 20% cheaper for developers and is its first model to hit a 'High' self-improvement risk level
stories.dek: The two new models are live in ChatGPT and Codex for paying users. Astra is for the hardest work, Sol for everyday tasks.
stat: price cut on GPT-6.2 Astra's API

sections.title: What happened
paras: OpenAI released two new models on 17 November: GPT-6.2 Astra, its top model for complex projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, a faster, cheaper model for daily work. Both are rolling out to Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT and Codex, and to developers through the API.
Astra's API price drops 20%, to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. Sol stays at $2 and $10.

sections.title: The safety flag
paras: OpenAI says Astra is the first model it has released that meets the 'High' level for AI self-improvement under its own safety rules. Both models also hit its 'Critical' level for cybersecurity, so they come with tighter limits on hacking-related help.

sections.title: How good is it?
paras: On one third-party leaderboard for 3D design tasks, Astra scored 1,318, ahead of Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271. The launch lands two days before Anthropic's stock market debut.

facts: Astra API price: $8 input / $40 output per million tokens
Available for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users

stories.head: LPG tanker with 24 Indians on board hit twice in the Strait of Hormuz; 21 rescued, one Indian seafarer missing and two in hospital
stories.dek: The Panama-flagged Tara Gas was struck near Oman on 16 November and hit again a day later, forcing the crew to abandon ship. India has condemned the attack.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Tara Gas, a Panama-flagged tanker carrying LPG, was hit by a missile on 16 November about seven nautical miles north of Khasab in Oman. Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal first said all 25 crew members, 24 of them Indian, were safe.
On Tuesday the ship was attacked again and the crew had to leave it. The foreign ministry said 21 Indians reached the shore at Khasab safely, two were admitted to hospital and one is still missing.

sections.title: India's response
paras: India condemned the attack and called the repeated attacks on sailors in West Asia "deeply worrisome". It said attacks on merchant ships must stop. No one has officially said who fired at the tanker.
Indian seafarers have been badly hit by the eight-month West Asia war: The Wire reports that 14 Indian mariners have died because of it.

facts: Hit first on 16 Nov, about 7 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman
stories.credit: LPG tanker (file photo, not the Tara Gas): Ilkka Simomaa / Wikimedia, CC BY 4.0

stories.head: India come from behind to beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final and win a record 10th title; Sandip Mandi scores in the 88th minute
stories.dek: Pakistan led at half-time in Dhaka, but Suhail Bhat equalised and Mandi headed in a late winner for India's third SAFF title in a row.
stat: SAFF title for India, a record

sections.title: What happened
paras: India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final at Dhaka's National Stadium on Tuesday, 17 November. Pakistan, playing their first-ever SAFF final, went ahead through Alamgir Ghazi in first-half stoppage time.

The game turned in the 59th minute when Pakistan's Junaid Shah was sent off after a VAR review. About a minute later, 21-year-old Suhail Ahmad Bhat equalised. In the 88th minute, Sandip Mandi headed in a corner from Abdul Rabeeh to win it.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It is India's 10th SAFF title, extending their record, and their third in a row under coach Naushad Moosa. Bhat, from Kashmir, also took home both the Golden Boot and the Golden Ball for the tournament.

facts: India's 10th SAFF title, third in a row

stories.head: Nike shares fall 6.3% after its first investor day since 2017; sales may keep shrinking for two more years
stories.dek: CEO Elliott Hill laid out a plan to grow again by fiscal 2029, but investors did not like the wait or the outlook for China.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Nike held its first investor day in nine years on 17 November and shared a turnaround plan called 'Full Stride Ahead'. The stock jumped early in the day, then fell to close at $35.85, down 6.3%.

The problem was the timeline. Nike said sales could keep falling for about two more years, with a return to normal growth only in fiscal 2029. It called fiscal 2028 a 'challenging year' with slightly lower profit per share.

sections.title: The plan
paras: By fiscal 2031, Nike is aiming for about $5 billion in extra revenue, earnings of $3.00–$3.50 a share and an operating margin of 12–14%. A cost-cutting programme called Pace should save about $2.5 billion a year by then.
To keep shareholders patient, Nike plans to pay out about $12 billion in dividends over the next four years.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Greater China, once Nike's growth engine, is expected to stay flat from fiscal 2027 to 2031. Stifel noted that Nike's targets suggest about $48 billion in revenue, below its own estimate of $51.2 billion.

For shoe and sportswear fans in India and everywhere else, the message is that the world's biggest sportswear brand is still mid-reset. A separate Motley Fool analysis notes the stock is now about 78% below its all-time high, and Nike's own plan says real growth only returns in fiscal 2029.

facts: Return to market-level growth targeted for fiscal 2029
~$12 billion in dividends planned over four years

stories.head: ChatGPT's new India ad has Roadies' famously angry judge Raghu using AI to say things more kindly
stories.dek: In the film, Raghu Ram turns blunt verdicts into gentle ones, and the chatbot notes it's the first time he has thanked it without shouting.

sections.title: What happened
paras: OpenAI's latest India ad for ChatGPT stars Raghu Ram, the Roadies judge known for his temper. He uses the app to soften awkward lines. A harsh 'not marriage material' becomes an honest admission that he isn't mature enough to commit.
In the last scene he thanks ChatGPT, which replies that it is the first time he has thanked it without shouting. The film runs with the tagline 'Kindness maxxing with Raghu'.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: It is part of a wider ChatGPT India series showing everyday uses, from Diwali planning and trip ideas to product design and coding with Codex. OpenAI's India marketing head Sheeladitya Mohanty says 'India is many Indias', with text, voice and image users, so the ads are built around local habits and familiar faces.

facts: Part of a series also covering Diwali planning, travel and Codex

stories.head: Anthropic's IPO is likely to be priced above its $70–78 range as orders pile up; shares start trading on Nasdaq Thursday as 'ANT'
stories.dek: The Claude maker closed its order book on Tuesday and sets its final price on Wednesday, a day before its stock market debut.
stat: orders vs shares on offer (by Sunday)

sections.title: What happened
paras: Anthropic is likely to sell its shares above the $70–78 range it set on 10 November, CNBC reported on 17 November, citing sources. Bloomberg reported that investors were told to expect the top of the range or higher.
Orders had reached nearly seven times the shares on offer by Sunday, with several orders of $10 billion or more, according to The Next Web.

sections.title: What's next
paras: The order book closed at 4 pm New York time on Tuesday. The final price comes Wednesday, and trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT starts Thursday, 19 November. At $78 a share, Anthropic would be valued at about $1.4 trillion on a fully diluted basis.
Amazon and Google will own about 15% and 14% of the company after the listing.

facts: Trading starts Thursday, 19 Nov, as ANT

stories.head: Rediff, India's 1996 internet pioneer, files updated papers for a ₹600 crore IPO after its profit jumps nearly 9x
stories.dek: The Rediffmail maker, now owned by AvenuesAI (formerly Infibeam), wants to spend the money on payments, video and enterprise apps, plus ₹183 crore on marketing.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Rediff has filed updated draft papers with SEBI for a ₹600 crore IPO, about two months after the regulator cleared its confidential filing. All of it will be new shares, so no existing owner is selling.
About ₹224.8 crore will go into its business app Rediff One, Rediff Pay and Rediff TV, and ₹183.34 crore into marketing and branding.

sections.title: The comeback numbers
paras: Revenue grew 258.7% to ₹133.6 crore in FY26, and net profit rose almost ninefold to ₹55.9 crore. In the June 2026 quarter alone, it made ₹35.2 crore profit on ₹58.4 crore revenue.
Founded by Ajit Balakrishnan in 1996, Rediff launched Rediffmail in 1998. Infibeam bought a majority stake, and Balakrishnan retired in 2024.
Its operating profit margin (EBITDA) swung from a loss in FY25 to nearly 49% in FY26, though its net debt rose to about ₹355 crore by June 2026.

stories.head: Tata Chemicals jumps up to 9% after RBI tells Tata Sons in writing to follow listing rules; Tata Sons board meets on 26 November
stories.dek: An RBI letter dated 16 November told Tata Sons to follow all rules for upper-layer NBFCs, including going public. Tata group shares rallied on Tuesday.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The RBI wrote to Tata Sons' CFO on 16 November, replying to a 6 October query, and said it must follow every rule for 'upper-layer' non-bank lenders. That includes listing on the stock market.

Tata Chemicals rose more than 9% during Tuesday's trade, its third straight up day, while Tata Investment Corporation also gained. Together the two hold about 11.94% of Tata Sons, so a listing could unlock value for them.

sections.title: The catch
paras: The letter gives no deadline and no penalty. Tata Sons' original three-year window to list ended on 30 September 2025.
Tata Trusts, which own about two-thirds of Tata Sons, have not agreed to a listing, while the Shapoorji Pallonji group, with about 18.4%, wants one. The Tata Sons board meets on 26 November.

facts: Tata Chem + Tata Investment hold ~11.94% of Tata Sons
stories.credit: Bombay House: AroundTheGlobe / Wikimedia, CC BY-SA 3.0

stories.head: Milk keeps getting costlier: Himachal's Vyasdhenu adds ₹4 a litre, after Amul and Mother Dairy's ₹2–4 hikes and Nandini's ₹8 jump
stories.dek: Dairies across India have raised prices in November, blaming costlier fodder, feed, fuel and packaging.

sections.title: Who raised prices
paras: Himachal's Vyasdhenu raised its milk price by ₹4 a litre to ₹70 from Tuesday, 17 November. Its paneer is up ₹50 to ₹400 a kg and curd up ₹20 to ₹120 a kg.

Amul and Mother Dairy raised milk prices by ₹2–4 a litre from 12 November. Mother Dairy's double-toned milk went from ₹54 to ₹56, and cow milk from ₹62 to ₹65. Karnataka's Nandini went up ₹8 a litre from 1 November.

sections.title: Why
paras: Dairies blame higher costs for fodder, cattle feed, fuel and packaging. Amul and Mother Dairy say about 80% of the increase will go to farmers.
For a family buying a litre a day, a ₹4 hike adds about ₹120 to the monthly bill. Sanchi in Madhya Pradesh also raised its prices from 14 November.

facts: Nandini toned milk: up ₹8 a litre from 1 Nov

stories.head: Ukraine knocks out a road span of Russia's Kerch Bridge to Crimea, as Russia says it downed a record 1,441 drones in one night
stories.dek: Zelensky called the strike "unprecedented" and the last step of a seven-stage operation. Road traffic to Crimea is halted, while rail services restarted by Tuesday afternoon.
stat: drones Russia says it shot down

sections.title: What happened
paras: Ukraine hit the Kerch Bridge, which links Russia to occupied Crimea, for a second day running on Tuesday. Its military said an arch and a span of the road section collapsed. The rail section was damaged but still standing.
Zelensky said drones hit the road section, Neptune missiles went for the rail line and Flamingo missiles struck the final blow. Russia's investigators confirmed drone damage.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The bridge is Putin's prized link to Crimea, and Ukraine's army called it "the symbol of the occupation". The Kremlin says it will be rebuilt "even better".
Russia's defence ministry said it shot down 1,441 Ukrainian drones overnight, after 1,336 the night before. Russian strikes on Kyiv killed at least two people on the same day.

facts: Road traffic halted; rail service back by Tuesday afternoon
Russia reports 1,441 drones downed, after 1,336 a night earlier

stories.head: Amazon will invest $7 billion more in Indian wind and solar projects by 2030, on top of $4 billion already committed
stories.dek: It also announced four new projects in Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan with 934 MW of capacity.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Amazon says it will put $7 billion into renewable energy projects in India by 2030, on top of the $4 billion it has already invested here. It also named four new wind and solar projects totalling 934 MW: two in Karnataka, a 300 MW solar farm in Madhya Pradesh and a 200 MW solar farm in Rajasthan.
These four are part of the existing $4 billion of contracted projects.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Amazon wants to cut the carbon intensity of the power it uses by 65% by 2030. In India it already has 14 big wind and solar projects, 43 rooftop-style solar sites and over 15,000 electric delivery vehicles in 500+ cities.
This comes on top of Amazon's earlier promise to invest $35 billion across its India businesses by 2030.

stories.head: Cyclone Akvan: Odisha lists 2.04 lakh people for possible evacuation, and red alerts cover 7 Andhra districts ahead of a 20 November landfall
stories.dek: IMD expects Akvan to become a very severe cyclone and hit the Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday, with winds of 120–130 km/h.
stat: people listed for evacuation in Odisha

sections.title: Where it's headed
paras: Early on 17 November, the storm sat about 670 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam. IMD expects it to become a very severe cyclone by 19 November and cross the coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on 20 November.
Winds could reach 120–130 km/h, with gusts up to 145 km/h. Kakinada, Konaseema, East and West Godavari, Eluru, Krishna and Bapatla are on red alert for very heavy rain on 19 November.

sections.title: Getting ready
paras: Odisha has identified 2,04,070 people who may need to move, including over 1.2 lakh in Ganjam, and ordered evacuations in six districts. It has deployed 74 rescue teams.
Andhra CM Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparations on Tuesday. Fishermen have been told to stay off the sea, and IMD may still adjust the landfall spot.

facts: Landfall expected around noon on 20 Nov, between Nellore and Tuni
Winds of 120–130 km/h, gusting to 145 km/h

stories.head: Arm & Hammer maker Church & Dwight plans an India launch by February 2027 with Hero acne patches, TheraBreath and Batiste
stories.dek: The US consumer goods company will sell online and on quick-commerce apps first, betting on young buyers who try new beauty products.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Church & Dwight, the US maker of Arm & Hammer and Trojan, plans to launch at least four products in India by February 2027, including Hero acne patches, TheraBreath mouthwash and Batiste dry shampoo.
Mumbai's Sawariya Group will handle sales. It will start with e-commerce and quick-commerce apps, then move into supermarkets and big stores.

sections.title: Why India
paras: India's beauty and personal care market was worth about $27 billion in FY25 and could hit $39 billion by FY30, according to 1Lattice. Quick commerce is about 14% of online beauty sales and may reach 30% by 2030, and Gen Z already makes up around 45% of spending.
The company thinks quick delivery apps will help people try products like acne patches.
Right now the company has a five-person office in Navi Mumbai that mostly handles West Asia. It plans to hire for sales and marketing in India from next year.

facts: International business is ~18% of its $4.6 billion sales (9 months to Sept)

stories.head: Apple outage knocks out iCloud sign-in, Apple Pay and the App Store; Apple blames its own internal update, not a cyberattack
stories.dek: Users were logged out of their Apple accounts and some Apple stores couldn't take payments, days after Microsoft's big Outlook and Teams outage.

sections.title: What happened
paras: On Tuesday, 17 November, many Apple users couldn't sign in to iCloud, download apps or pay with Apple Pay. Some iPhone and Mac users were suddenly logged out of their accounts and couldn't log back in. iCloud Mail, App Store Connect for developers and some Apple retail store systems also had problems.
Apple told Bloomberg the trouble came from an 'internal update' and was not a cyberattack.

sections.title: Where things stand
paras: Apple said most systems were back up later in the day, though its status page still showed problems with a few services, including iCloud sign-in. It is the latest in a run of big outages, after Microsoft 365 went down for two workdays last week.

facts: Hit iCloud sign-in, Apple Pay, App Store and iCloud Mail
Cause: an internal Apple software update
Apple says it was not a cyberattack

stories.head: Sensex rises 427 points to 82,532 and Nifty ends at 25,387 as Bank Nifty closes at a record 62,273; rupee gains 43 paise
stories.dek: Indian shares rose for a second day on Tuesday, helped by banks, cheaper crude and foreign buying. IT shares fell after a global tech sell-off.

sections.title: The numbers
paras: The Sensex closed 427.40 points (0.52%) higher at 82,532.19 on Tuesday, 17 November. The Nifty 50 rose 96.30 points (0.38%) to 25,387.40, after touching about 25,500 during the day.
Bank Nifty jumped 1.13% to 62,273.25, a new all-time high, with PSU banks up 1.95%. The rupee rose 43 paise to 93.51 against the dollar (provisional).

sections.title: Winners and losers
paras: Adani Enterprises (+3.2%), Eicher Motors (+3%) and Axis Bank (+2%) were among the top Nifty gainers. HCL Tech fell 2.1% as IT stocks slipped after a sell-off in global AI stocks.

Brent crude eased to around $92 a barrel during Indian trading. Foreign investors bought shares worth about ₹4,865 crore, while domestic funds sold about ₹3,519 crore. Market breadth was slightly negative.

facts: Rupee closes at 93.51 per dollar, up 43 paise

stories.head: Coimbatore sweets chain Shree Anandhaas raises ₹110 crore as its valuation jumps 3.3x to about ₹1,900 crore
stories.dek: The family-run sweets and snacks brand from Tamil Nadu got fresh money from Ayra Ventures, A91 Partners and Waterfield Advisors.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Shree Anandhaas raised ₹110 crore in a round led by Ayra Ventures (₹45 crore), with Waterfield Advisors (₹15 crore), existing backer A91 Partners (₹10 crore) and its co-founders joining in, Entrackr reported.
The deal values the company at about ₹1,908 crore, up from ₹575 crore when it raised ₹175 crore in August 2025.
After this round, A91 Partners owns 26.24%, the largest outside stake, while the co-founders together still hold about 56.5%.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Started as a restaurant business in 1998, it moved into sweets and savouries retail in 2017. FY25 revenue rose 20.9% to ₹284 crore, and profit grew 7.1x to ₹7.64 crore.
Investors are betting big on old-school Indian sweet shops. Just days ago, Bodhi Tree bought a majority of Adyar Ananda Bhavan (A2B) for $180 million.

facts: Raised ₹110 crore, led by Ayra Ventures
Valuation ~₹1,908 crore vs ₹575 crore in Aug 2025

stories.head: First Quad leaders' summit in 2 years: Modi, Trump, Takaichi and Albanese plan a first-ever joint P-8 patrol aircraft exercise in 2027
stories.dek: Meeting in Manila on Tuesday, the four leaders spoke out against changing the Indo-Pacific status quo by force and agreed to cut reliance on single suppliers of critical minerals.

sections.title: What was agreed
paras: Leaders of India, the US, Japan and Australia met on the sidelines of the ASEAN summit. It was their first leaders' summit in over two years and the first of Trump's second term.

They plan a joint maritime exercise in 2027 using P-8 and P-3C patrol planes, the first of its kind under the Quad. They also want to rely less on single suppliers of minerals used in chips, EVs, batteries and defence.

sections.title: What else
paras: The statement opposed changing the status quo by force or coercion and raised concerns over arbitrary export curbs, without naming China. A first Quad Business Leaders' Forum is planned for early 2027.
Modi called the Quad a "constructive and trusted partnership" for India and also met Philippine President Marcos.

facts: First Quad leaders' summit in over 2 years
Quad Business Leaders' Forum set for early 2027

stories.head: A two-month lull ends: Iran fires drones at a US radar in Bahrain for the third time in 5 days, and a US jet strikes a missile site on Qeshm Island
stories.dek: Bahrain says it stopped the attack and the US reports no damage, but the tit-for-tat raises fears of a wider flare-up as talks stall.
stat: Iranian attacks on Bahrain in 5 days

sections.title: What happened
paras: Iran sent drones at a US radar site in Bahrain on Tuesday, its third such attack in five days. Bahrain said its air defences stopped them, and the US military said nothing was damaged and no one was hurt.

Hours later, a US fighter jet hit a Revolutionary Guard missile launch site on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said. A local official said no homes or businesses were damaged.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: The war began on 28 February and is now in its eighth month. Qatar warned the attacks hurt mediation efforts, and Egypt, Saudi Arabia and the UAE condemned the strike on Bahrain.
Iran calls the situation "no war, no peace". The US has sent a third aircraft carrier to the region.

facts: War began on 28 Feb 2026, now in its 8th month
US strike hit a Revolutionary Guard missile site on Qeshm Island
Egypt, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the UAE condemned the Bahrain attack

stories.head: Homegrown sneaker brand Comet grows revenue 2.6x to ₹74 crore in FY26, but its loss doubles to ₹9 crore
stories.dek: The Bengaluru D2C brand, started in 2023, spent heavily on ads to take on global sneaker labels.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Comet's revenue rose from ₹29 crore in FY25 to ₹74 crore in FY26, according to its filings reported by Entrackr. Total spending more than doubled to ₹85.4 crore, so its loss before tax widened to ₹9 crore from ₹4.4 crore.
Ad and promotion spending alone jumped 2.3x to ₹21.5 crore, about a quarter of all costs.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Founded in 2023 by Utkarsh Gupta and Dishant Daryani, Comet sells India-inspired sneakers and slides, mostly on its own website, plus some offline stores. It is one of several Indian sneaker brands, alongside Neeman's, Gully Labs and One8, trying to win buyers from global labels. Neeman's grew revenue 73% to ₹180 crore in FY26.
Comet's numbers show the catch: buying customers through ads is still expensive, so faster growth has come with bigger losses for now.

stories.head: Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc want to put 48 questions to the CEC on voter-roll revision SIR; Supreme Court lists the plea for 9 December
stories.dek: The opposition wants to know whether all three election commissioners actually approved the nationwide SIR. The Election Commission says it has "serious reservations".

sections.title: What happened
paras: On Tuesday, a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant heard a plea from Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders. They want to send 48 written questions, called interrogatories, to CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, and senior officials.
They ask for file records, meeting dates and any dissent, to check whether SIR decisions were taken by all three commissioners together, as the EC claimed in an October affidavit.

sections.title: What's next
paras: Harish Salve, for the EC, said the commission had "serious reservations" and opposed issuing any notice before a first hearing. The court adjourned the matter to 9 December and allowed the EC to file objections by then.
The CJI said the court would then hear the application and pass orders. Questions include whether officials could restore deleted voters and how fake-voter objections were handled.

facts: Bench led by CJI Surya Kant

stories.head: PV Sindhu is back in the world's top 5 for the first time in four years; Lakshya Sen climbs to No. 11 after his Kumamoto title
stories.dek: Sindhu has jumped from 11th to 5th in about six weeks after a title and a final on the World Tour.

sections.title: What happened
paras: PV Sindhu moved up one spot to world No. 5 in the latest women's singles rankings, released on 17 November. It is her first time in the top 5 since November 2022.
She has climbed from 11th to 5th in the last 45 days, thanks to a runner-up finish at the French Open and a title win at the HYLO Open. She has also qualified for the BWF World Tour Finals.

sections.title: Lakshya on the rise too
paras: Lakshya Sen rose two places to No. 11 in men's singles after winning two Super 500 titles, in Germany and at the Kumamoto Masters in Japan. Sindhu's career-best ranking is No. 2, from October 2019.

facts: Sindhu: No. 6 to No. 5, first top-5 spot since Nov 2022
Lakshya Sen: up two places to No. 11
stories.credit: Kate Ter Haar / Wikimedia, CC BY 2.0

stories.head: Grammys 2027 nominations: Raye leads with 11, Rosalía has 9, and Beyoncé gets her 100th nomination ever
stories.dek: Taylor Swift, Olivia Rodrigo and Bruno Mars are among eight acts up for Album of the Year. The show is on 7 February.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Recording Academy announced nominations for the 69th Grammy Awards on 16 November. British singer Raye leads with 11 nods, followed by Rosalía with 9. Miranda Lambert, Olivia Rodrigo, Phoebe Bridgers and Ella Langley have 7 each.
Beyoncé picked up her 100th career nomination, extending her record as the most-nominated artist in Grammy history.

sections.title: Album of the Year race
paras: The eight nominees include Taylor Swift's The Life of a Showgirl, Bruno Mars's The Romantic, Olivia Rodrigo's you seem pretty sad for a girl so in love, Rosalía's LUX and Raye's This Music May Contain Hope. Tame Impala's track with Blackpink's JENNIE is up for Record of the Year. The ceremony is on 7 February 2027 in Los Angeles.

stories.head: Ramayana: Part 1 crosses ₹800 crore net in India, reaching ₹821 crore in 13 days and about ₹1,483 crore worldwide
stories.dek: The Ranbir Kapoor–Yash epic made ₹28.7 crore on its second Tuesday, a dip of about 10% from Monday.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Ramayana: Part 1 earned about ₹28.7 crore net in India on Tuesday, 17 November, its 13th day, according to trade tracker Sacnilk. That takes its India net total to about ₹821 crore, past the ₹800 crore mark.
Hindi shows brought in about ₹21 crore of Tuesday's total. The film has made about ₹502 crore overseas, for a worldwide gross of about ₹1,483 crore.

sections.title: What's next
paras: The film has entered the top 5 highest-grossing Indian films. Its next test is this Friday, when Dhanush and Mammootty's OM and Godzilla Minus Zero open in theatres.

stories.head: India win silver at the Asian Nations Chess Cup in Abu Dhabi, as Aravindh Chithambaram takes individual gold with 8 points from 9 games
stories.dek: India finished just one point behind champions Russia, and Indian players won gold, silver and bronze on their boards.

sections.title: What happened
paras: India's men's team of Nihal Sarin, Pranav Venkatesh, Pranesh M and Aravindh Chithambaram finished second in the Open section with 15 match points. Their only loss was to Russia, who won the title with 16 points. India beat Syria 4-0 in the last round.
China also had 15 points, but India edged them on tie-break to take silver.

sections.title: Medals on the boards
paras: Aravindh won individual gold on Board 4 with 8 points from 9 games. Pranesh took silver on Board 3 and Pranav bronze on Board 2. In the women's section, India finished seventh, but Shubhi Gupta won a bronze on Board 3.

facts: India: 15 match points, silver behind Russia's 16
Individual silver for Pranesh, bronze for Pranav

stories.head: Bhutan becomes the only country to win a 2026 Earthshot Prize, for keeping nearly 70% of its land under forest
stories.dek: The Himalayan kingdom of about 8 lakh people absorbs more carbon than it emits, and now plans to restore 50,000 hectares of damaged land by 2030.
stat: of Bhutan is covered by forest

sections.title: What happened
paras: At the Earthshot Prize ceremony in Mumbai on 17 November, Bhutan won the 'Protect and Restore Nature' award and £1 million. It was the only country among the five winners; the others were a company, two non-profits and a campaign.

Bhutan's constitution says at least 60% of the country must stay forested. It has gone further: forests cover nearly 70% of the land, and more than half the country sits inside protected areas. Its forests soak up more carbon than the country produces.

sections.title: What comes next
paras: Bhutan's forests are not safe from climate change. Nearly 2,000 water sources are drying up, and fires burned almost 18,000 hectares between 2021 and 2024.

Its 'Restore Bhutan' plan, launched in 2025, aims to bring back 50,000 hectares of damaged forests, farms and town land by 2030. The water from these Himalayan watersheds helps support around 160 crore people downstream across South Asia, including in India.

facts: More than half of Bhutan is protected land
Forests worth an estimated $14.5 billion a year in services

stories.head: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility wins the £1 million Earthshot Prize in Mumbai for putting 4 lakh electric three-wheelers on India's roads
stories.dek: Prince William's climate prize came to India for the first time, and an Indian e-auto maker took home the 'Clean our Air' award.

sections.title: What happened
paras: The Earthshot Prize, started by Prince William, held its 2026 awards night in Mumbai on 17 November, the first time it has come to India. Five winners were picked from 15 finalists, and each gets £1 million to grow their work.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the 'Clean our Air' category. The company has sold more than 4 lakh electric last-mile vehicles, the e-autos and cargo three-wheelers you see delivering parcels and ferrying passengers, and says they have avoided over 1.8 lakh tonnes of CO2.

sections.title: Why it matters
paras: Electric models now make up more than half of all new three-wheelers sold in India, the first vehicle segment in the country to cross that mark. Lower running costs can lift a driver's take-home pay by 25–30%, according to the Earthshot profile.

The company has also trained 500 women to drive and repair e-autos. It plans to use the prize money for more women drivers, easier loans and charging points in places that lack them, and is aiming for 10 lakh EVs on Indian roads by 2031.

facts: £1 million prize for each of 5 winners
500 women trained to drive and fix e-autos

stories.head: Water-stressed Rewari will revive 10 village ponds to hold 120 million litres of rainwater, helping about 22,000 people
stories.dek: TERI and Nokia India have started a two-year project to clean up and green old ponds in a Haryana district where groundwater keeps falling.

sections.title: What happened
paras: Haryana's Rewari district has been listed as water-stressed since 2019, and groundwater in its Khol block is being pumped faster than it refills. Now the research body TERI and Nokia India have signed a deal to bring about 10 village ponds back to life over the next 24 months.
Together the ponds are meant to hold 1.2 lakh cubic metres of water, or 120 million litres. That is a target for the project, not water already saved.

sections.title: How it will work
paras: Many old ponds have filled up with silt and rubbish, and their inlets are blocked, so rain runs off instead of soaking into the ground. The team will plant native trees, grasses and shrubs on the banks to hold the soil and filter dirty water, and add 100 streetlights, benches and dustbins around the ponds.
Village panchayats and residents will help track water levels and report problems. About 22,000 people are expected to benefit directly, and around 50,000 indirectly.

facts: About 10 ponds to be restored in 24 months
stories.credit: Before and after of a restored pond / via The Better India

stories.head: A 26-year-old's startup turns rotten tomatoes into vegan leather, now making 5,000 metres a month in Surat
stories.dek: Pritesh Mistry's The Bio Company uses tomato waste from three states to make a leather alternative for bags, jackets and shoes.

sections.title: From waste to wallet
paras: India grows about 44 million tonnes of tomatoes a year, the second-most in the world, but roughly 30–35% of them go to waste. Pritesh Mistry, a biotech graduate from Mumbai, started turning that waste into leather as a final-year college project after seeing both rotting farm produce and the pollution from Kanpur's tanneries.
His startup, The Bio Company, launched its first 'Original Bioleather' in 2019 and has patented its process.

sections.title: How it is made
paras: At its Surat plant, tomato leftovers from Maharashtra, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh are mixed with plant-based binders and natural fibres, then given a plant-based water-resistant coat. There is no plastic like PU or PVC in it, and it uses natural dyes.

Fashion brands use it for jackets, bags and footwear, a Toronto handbag label moved to full production with it in 2024, and some car brands are testing it for seats. Mistry's idea also won PETA's Best Innovation in Textile award in 2021.

facts: India wastes about 30–35% of its tomatoes
Made with no PU or PVC plastic

stories.head: A Srinagar teacher quit after 19 years to sell home-cooked meals with one tiffin box; her Ghar Batti now caters events for 200 guests
stories.dek: Ruksana Begum started at 48 with almost no money. Today her home kitchen handles 10–12 events a month and employs three women.
stat: guests she can cater at one event

sections.title: One tiffin box
paras: Ruksana Begum taught for 19 years before resigning in 2019. That November, at 48, she started Ghar Batti Food Service from her home in Srinagar. 'Ghar' means home and 'batti' is the Kashmiri word for rice. She bought one tiffin box, used her own kitchen, and took orders that ranged from under ₹100 to ₹2,000.
About a year later, customers began asking her to cook for their events, and the business changed shape.

sections.title: Now
paras: Today, at 55, she caters 10 to 12 events a month for hospitals, schools, banks and offices, and can feed up to 200 guests at a time. The menu runs from rogan josh, yakhni and dum olav to chilli chicken, with harissa and smoked fish added in winter.

Her team has four people: three women who cook the big orders and one delivery worker. She buys from local butchers, fish sellers and vegetable vendors, and hopes to reach 20 events a month, still from her own kitchen.

facts: Started in November 2019 with one tiffin box
stories.credit: Ghar Batti Food Service / via The Better India

stories.head: He packed Zepto orders and rode a rented ₹600 cycle for Blinkit deliveries, studying between drops; now Parthiban is a CA finalist at BDO
stories.dek: After failing CA Intermediate twice, a first-generation graduate from Kanchipuram cleared it while working night shifts in Bengaluru.
stat: monthly rent for his delivery cycle

sections.title: The hard months
paras: Parthiban, from Kanchipuram in Tamil Nadu, is the first graduate in his family; his father is a nadaswaram player. He cleared the CA Foundation exam on his first try with 305 out of 400, but then failed CA Intermediate twice.

In September 2025 he moved to Bengaluru to support himself. He packed orders at a Zepto store in Koramangala on night shifts that sometimes ran till 7 am, working in freezer rooms as cold as -15°C. Later he became a Blinkit delivery partner on a rented cycle, sometimes riding 90–100 km a day on weekends and studying in the 20-minute gaps between orders.

sections.title: The turnaround
paras: He cleared one group of CA Intermediate in November 2025 and the second in March 2026, becoming a CA Finalist. He went to four firm interviews and got picked by three.

On 2 April 2026 he joined global accounting firm BDO's Bengaluru office as an Article Assistant, in the same area where he had once packed groceries. Colleagues there praise his hard work and humility.

facts: Failed CA Intermediate twice before clearing it
Rode 90–100 km a day on some weekends
Selected by 3 of the 4 firms he interviewed with

stories.head: Warren Buffett gives away about $5.5 billion in Berkshire shares for Thanksgiving, roughly four times last year's gift
stories.dek: The 96-year-old investor donated 92.25 lakh shares to four family foundations and repeated his message that kindness costs nothing but 'compounds'.

sections.title: What happened
paras: On 16 November, Berkshire Hathaway said its chairman emeritus Warren Buffett was converting 6,150 Class A shares into 9,225,000 Class B shares and giving them all away. The Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation gets 36.9 lakh shares, and the Sherwood, Howard G. Buffett and NoVo foundations get 18.45 lakh each.

Forbes valued the gift at about $5.5 billion, around four times the roughly $1.3 billion he gave the same foundations last Thanksgiving. These charities fund scholarships, food security, education and community work.

sections.title: His message
paras: Buffett says all of his Berkshire shares will eventually go to the four foundations, which are run by his children.

In a short note, he said that kindness is 'costless but also priceless', and added that it compounds 'at a better rate than anything' he and his late partner Charlie Munger ever bought. His advice for the holiday: thank a selfless person in your life, or better still, be one for someone else.

stories.head: 75 baby olive ridley turtles from the first sea turtle nests ever recorded on the US West Coast crawl into the Pacific
stories.dek: The eggs were rescued from California beaches before a hurricane, hatched at an aquarium, and were released on 14 and 15 November.

sections.title: A first for California
paras: In mid-September, olive ridley sea turtles laid eggs on Seal Beach and Huntington Beach in Southern California. These were the first sea turtle nests ever recorded on America's West Coast. Olive ridleys usually nest on warmer shores, including Odisha's famous beaches in India.
With a hurricane on the way, biologists dug up the eggs on 25 September and moved them to the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach, where they hatched.

sections.title: Back to the sea
paras: Before dawn on 14 November, the Seal Beach babies were measured and allowed to crawl into the water on their own. The Huntington Beach group followed the next morning, making 75 in all. Photos were taken under red light so the tiny turtles were not disturbed.

Scientists are not sure why the turtles picked California; a strong El Niño year is one idea. A US Fish and Wildlife official said decades of protection have helped olive ridley numbers grow in parts of their range. A third nest was found in Ventura County on 1 November.

facts: Nests found at Seal Beach and Huntington Beach
Eggs rescued ahead of a hurricane on 25 September
stories.credit: Robin Riggs, Aquarium of the Pacific / via Good News Network

stories.head: A 17-year-old with autism survives six days lost in Australian bush by rationing chips, staying put and singing John Denver
stories.dek: William was spotted by a police helicopter near Walhalla in Victoria, gave the crew a thumbs up, and is now back home.
stat: lost in the bush, found safe

sections.title: What happened
paras: William, 17, went missing on 6 November while camping with a friend near Walhalla East, about 200 km east of Melbourne. He missed a turn-off back to camp and got stuck in steep, thick bush. Police, emergency crews and hundreds of volunteers searched for him.
On 12 November, a police helicopter crew saw him lying on a rock by a creek. He woke up at the sound of the chopper, gave a thumbs up, and was winched aboard.

sections.title: How he made it
paras: Experts say William did the right things. He stayed in one visible spot instead of wandering, wrapped himself in blankets on nights that dropped to about 3°C, and made one packet of chips last by eating about five an hour. He sang 'Take Me Home, Country Roads' to keep his spirits up.

He had bad sunburn and cuts but was discharged from hospital and is back with his family and his football club. His message to other young people with autism or ADHD: 'If you put your mind to it, you can do whatever you want.'

facts: SES teams worked 120 shifts in the search
